prompt.en: A balanced-output tuner is replaced by one with only an unbalanced output. The window line and dipole are unchanged. Which new boundary needs attention?

text.en: The coax-to-tuner input, because every tuner input is balanced.

feedback.en: The stated new input is coax. The new balance transition is at the output feeding balanced line.

text.en: Only the dipole feed point after the balanced-line run.

feedback.en: The balanced line and dipole are already balanced. The changed boundary is earlier.

text.en: The new tuner output feeding the existing balanced line.

feedback.en: The replacement creates an unbalanced-to-balanced transition before the window line begins.

text.en: The midpoint of the window line, to equalize losses in its two halves.

feedback.en: Equal cable halves do not define a balance transition. Follow the electrical boundary instead.

explanation.en: A replacement component can create a new interface requirement even if the antenna itself stays unchanged.

prompt.en: A coax jumper will be wound tightly on a ferrite toroid for common-mode control. Which dielectric choice follows the construction guidance?

text.en: Choose foam only because lower loss guarantees better resistance to tight bending.

feedback.en: Low loss and mechanical stability are different properties. Foam does not give that guarantee.

text.en: Prefer solid dielectric to help keep the centre conductor from shifting toward the shield.

feedback.en: Solid dielectric supports the conductor during tight winding, reducing the risk of a short.

text.en: Choose the thinnest insulation because the shield alone keeps the conductor centred.

feedback.en: The dielectric separates and supports the conductors. Thinner insulation is not automatically safer.

text.en: Treat foam and solid dielectric as mechanically identical if both cables have the same Z0.

feedback.en: Equal characteristic impedance does not establish identical mechanical behaviour under tight winding.

explanation.en: Choose cable for its mechanical job as well as attenuation and characteristic impedance.

prompt.en: A new coax sample has the same length and DC conductor resistance as an old one, but a different dielectric. Which RF property may differ?

text.en: Only the maximum current, because RF propagation ignores insulation.

feedback.en: Dielectric affects RF wave speed and characteristic impedance, not just current rating.

text.en: Only total attenuation, because equal length fixes characteristic impedance.

feedback.en: Length does not fix Z0. Geometry and dielectric do.

text.en: No RF property, because an ohmmeter comparison is sufficient.

feedback.en: A DC ohmmeter does not measure characteristic impedance or propagation speed.
Dielectric helps set wave speed and Z0. Equal DC resistance does not make two RF lines equivalent.

explanation.en: RF feedlines need more specifications than length and DC resistance.
